subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should OpenClaw solve this direct `read`-tool token waste now with a safe binary-document fallback, or defer it to broader document extraction/provider-native file handling?
rationale: Source inspection proves the direct fallback is still missing, but the issue proposes multiple product directions and has an open conflicting PR, so automation should not choose the permanent behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Port Safe Fallback
options.body: Add a small guard for known binary document formats in the shared `read` path and return a compact actionable unsupported-document message.

options.title: Defer To Document Work
options.body: Keep this issue tied to broader document extraction/provider-native file handling and accept that direct `read` can still waste tokens until that work lands.

options.title: Guidance Only
options.body: Update tool description or prompting to discourage binary document reads without changing runtime behavior.

recommendation.title: Port Safe Fallback
recommendation.body: Add a small guard for known binary document formats in the shared `read` path and return a compact actionable unsupported-document message.

likelyOwner.reason: The current checkout ties the active read-tool files to `joshavant`, making them the best available routing candidate from local history.
